full_text_en:
Heilongjiang Mincheng Investment Group Co., Ltd. v. Xilin Steel Group Co., Ltd. and Third Party Liu Zhiping — dispute over private lending

【Ruling Summary】

Whether a private lending contract has been formed, taken effect, and been fully performed in practice should be assessed from the perspectives of both contract execution and performance. The lender should provide evidence such as the loan agreement, bank transaction records, and reconciliation records to prove the fact, and the relevant evidence should be mutually corroborative.

Where the parties use the form of an equity transfer agreement to secure a private lending claim, this atypical security method constitutes transfer-for-security (rangyu guaranty). Provided that it does not violate the mandatory provisions on validity of laws and administrative regulations, the relevant equity transfer agreement is valid. After a transfer-for-security agreement on equity is entered into and the change of equity registration is completed in accordance with the agreement, if, due to the borrower's failure to repay the loan on schedule, the parties then agree to evaluate the target company's equity and assets, offset the corresponding amount of claims, confirm the validity of the previous equity change, and actually transfer control of the target company, it should be determined that the parties have reached a mutual agreement to genuinely transfer the equity and have actually performed it. If the borrower only initiates reorganization proceedings one year after this starting point, the borrower's claim to revoke the debt-for-equity transaction under the relevant provisions of the Bankruptcy Law should not be supported.

Regarding whether a transfer-for-security over equity has real right effect, the core criterion is whether the public notice principle of real rights has been followed. In an equity pledge, the pledgee may obtain priority satisfaction from the equity on which the pledge registration has been completed. In a transfer-for-security over equity where the equity as security property has been changed in registration to the name of the security holder, the security holder is formally the holder of the shares that are the subject of the security, and its right to priority satisfaction from the equity held as security should be even more protected. In principle, it enjoys the real right effect of being opposable to third parties. When the borrower enters reorganization proceedings, confirming that the transfer-for-security holder enjoys the right to priority satisfaction does not constitute individual satisfaction prohibited by Article 16 of the Bankruptcy Law.

Where a transfer-for-security over equity is established and the registration change is completed, and then the transfer-for-security holder consents to use that equity to secure a third party's claim against the debtor and completes the pledge registration, the third party shall be satisfied from that equity in priority to the transfer-for-security holder.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) SPC Civil Final No. 133

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Heilongjiang Mincheng Investment Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 2111, No. 242 Hongqi Street, Nangang Centralized Area, Harbin Economic and Technological Development Zone, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Ji Xuemei, Chairwoman and General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Xuefang, lawyer of Heilongjiang Xiangce Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wen Yong, lawyer of Liaoning Xinhe Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Xilin Steel Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Xinxing Street, Xilin District, Yichun City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Miao Qingyuan, Chairman of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xiaoxia, lawyer of Beijing Tianchi Juntai Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Dan, lawyer of Beijing Tianchi Juntai Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Liu Zhiping, male, born on December 24, 1958, Han ethnicity, domiciled at Daowai District, Harbin City, Heilongjiang Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Zhongqi, lawyer of Beijing Kenbang Law Firm.

Appellant Heilongjiang Mincheng Investment Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mincheng Company), in connection with the dispute over a private lending contract with Appellant Xilin Steel Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xigang Company) and Third Party at First Instance Liu Zhiping, appealed against the Civil Judgment (2017) Hei Civil First Instance No. 154 rendered by the Heilongjiang High People's Court. This Court accepted the appeal on January 21, 2019, and formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to hear the case in open court. The agents ad litem of Mincheng Company, Chen Xuefang and Wen Yong; the agents ad litem of Xigang Company, Zhang Xiaoxia and Wang Dan; and the agent ad litem of the Third Party at First Instance, Liu Zhiping, Zhang Zhongqi, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case has now been concluded.

Mincheng Company submitted an appeal to this Court, requesting: (1) to set aside Item 2 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2017) Hei Civil First Instance No. 154 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court; (2) to confirm that the transfer-for-security of the 64% equity held by Liu Zhiping in Xunke County Cuihongshan Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Cuihongshan Company) is lawful and valid, and to request priority satisfaction of all the principal and interest of Mincheng Company's loans from the proceeds obtained through discount, auction, or sale of the said 64% equity; (3) to order Xigang Company to bear all litigation costs, evaluation fees, and preservation fees in this case. Main reasons: (A) The first instance judgment failed to confirm the lawful validity of the transfer-for-security involved, which violates legal provisions and seriously infringes on the legitimate rights and interests of Mincheng Company. First, according to the Loan Agreement, the true intention of Liu Zhiping and Xigang Company was to transfer the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company owned by Xigang Company to the name of Liu Zhiping as security for the debt, which is a transfer-for-security, a widely used atypical security method. Second, the purpose of establishing a transfer-for-security is to enable the creditor to obtain priority satisfaction from the subject matter of the security when the debt is not performed. When Xigang Company is unable to perform its repayment obligation, the creditor has the right, through liquidation, to obtain priority satisfaction from the proceeds after the sale and discount of the secured subject matter. The first instance court's failure to support this claim is erroneous. Third, the security property involved has been registered in the name of Liu Zhiping with the industrial and commercial authorities, which has the effect of public notice of real rights and the effect of being opposable to third parties. It can restrict the transfer or other forms of disposal of the equity. Formally, Liu Zhiping has obtained the ownership of the security property and has priority effect excluding third parties. (B) The first instance judgment erred in the application of law, improperly depriving Mincheng Company of the right to claim priority satisfaction from the equity involved, and should be corrected. The first instance judgment held that if Mincheng Company were to obtain priority satisfaction from the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company, it would violate Article 16 of the Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Bankruptcy Law"), which provides that after the court accepts an application, any satisfaction of debts by the debtor to individual creditors is invalid. This is an erroneous application of law and an incorrect interpretation of the relevant provisions of the Bankruptcy Law. There are two reasons: First, the security arrangement between Mincheng Company (i.e., Liu Zhiping) and Xigang Company was not agreed upon and implemented after Xigang Company filed for bankruptcy or after the court accepted the bankruptcy application; rather, it was agreed upon as early as 2014 and actually performed. The first instance judgment recognized the above facts. Therefore, the first instance erroneously confused the security arrangement and priority satisfaction agreed between Mincheng Company (i.e., Liu Zhiping) and Xigang Company with the satisfaction to general creditors after bankruptcy, leading to the incorrect application of Article 16 of the Bankruptcy Law to the security arrangement at issue. Second, Mincheng Company's (i.e., Liu Zhiping's) security arrangement involved in this case should be protected according to law in the bankruptcy proceedings of Xigang Company. Pursuant to Article 109 of the Bankruptcy Law, Mincheng Company is a holder of security rights over specific property of the bankrupt, Xigang Company, and is entitled to priority satisfaction from that specific property. Any part not fully satisfied shall be treated as an ordinary claim. The right of priority satisfaction grants the secured creditor the right to obtain satisfaction from the proceeds of discount, auction, or sale of the secured property in priority to other creditors. The first instance court erroneously applied the law and unlawfully deprived Mincheng Company of the statutory right of priority satisfaction based on a lawful and valid security interest, seriously infringing on Mincheng Company's legitimate rights and interests. On February 11, 2019, Mincheng Company submitted a "Petition to Add Appeal Requests" to this Court, requesting that the interest on the loan amount of RMB 875,000,000 be calculated at the annual rate of 23.5% before tax in phases, increasing the interest amount by RMB 216,967,465.75. The main reason was: Xigang Company has already become bankrupt and cannot fulfill its tax payment obligations according to the judgment. After inquiring with the tax authorities, it was learned that Xigang Company cannot pay taxes. The taxpayer, Mincheng Company, must pay all taxes first, and may then seek recourse against the counterparty of the tax payment. Given the bankruptcy of Xigang Company, Mincheng Company cannot realize the possibility of recourse. Before the court hearing, Mincheng Company withdrew this newly added claim. During the second instance court hearing, Mincheng Company's agent ad litem stated, "When the contract was signed, it should have been considered that the taxpayer should be Mincheng Company, but Xigang Company should be the withholding agent. The first instance judgment supported the after-tax amount of 18%. Previously, during the appeal process, we also considered whether Xigang Company, being in the process of bankruptcy reorganization, still had the ability to withhold and pay. We hope the collegial panel will consider the issue of the taxpayer and actual burden."

Xigang Company argued in defense that Mincheng Company does not have the right to priority satisfaction over the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company, and that the first instance court correctly held that the transfer-for-security agreed between Xigang Company and Mincheng Company and Liu Zhiping had no real right effect and could not be opposed to third parties. (A) The agreement between Xigang Company and Mincheng Company regarding the transfer-for-security of Cuihongshan Company's equity constituted conduct to conceal or transfer assets for the purpose of evading debts and should be declared invalid. In June 2014, Xigang Company was already in severe operational difficulties, facing the risk of asset seizure and execution. To retain high-quality assets and evade satisfaction to other creditors, Xigang Company transferred its equity in Cuihongshan Company to Liu Zhiping, the representative of Mincheng Company, in the form of a transfer-for-security, which constitutes concealment or transfer of assets to evade debts. On June 11, 2018, Xigang Company formally entered bankruptcy proceedings. Therefore, this case should apply Article 33 of the Bankruptcy Law. (B) The transfer-for-security in this case cannot create priority satisfaction effect. First, transfer-for-security violates the principle of numerus clausus of real rights and the principle of public notice of real rights. Neither the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Property Law") nor the Security Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Security Law") provides for transfer-for-security. Only the types of real rights explicitly provided for in the Property Law and other laws may be recognized by law and have real right effect. Transfer-for-security, as an agreement between the parties, can create a contractual effect but cannot produce the same real right effect as a mortgage, pledge, or lien, cannot be opposed to third parties, and cannot obtain priority satisfaction over other creditors. Second, from the content of the contract, Mincheng Company cannot enjoy the right of priority satisfaction over Cuihongshan Company's equity. The Agreement signed between Mincheng Company and Xigang Company in June 2014 did not stipulate that the consequence of the transfer-for-security was priority satisfaction. It stipulated that if Xigang Company could not repay the debt, Liu Zhiping would become a shareholder of Cuihongshan Company. This clause constitutes a typical "forfeiture clause" (liuzhi contract) and should be invalid. The Supplemental Agreement signed in August 2015 stipulated that Liu Zhiping had the right to sell the equity of Cuihongshan Company to a third party if Xigang Company could not repay the debt, but it also did not stipulate that Liu Zhiping had the right to priority satisfaction. Third, transfer-for-security in bankruptcy does not enjoy the same effect of separation right (biechuquan) as statutory security interests. According to Article 109 of the Bankruptcy Law and the interpretation of that provision by the Legislative Affairs Commission of the National People's Congress, those entitled to priority satisfaction in bankruptcy proceedings are strictly limited to holders of statutory security interests under the Property Law and the Security Law, and do not include holders of other atypical security rights. Fourth, Liu Zhiping has pledged the equity he formally holds in Cuihongshan Company. In December 2014, Liu Zhiping entered into a "Maximum Amount Guaranty Contract" with China Minsheng Banking Corporation Limited, Dalian Branch (hereinafter "Minsheng Bank Dalian Branch"), pledging the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company held by Liu Zhiping and completing the equity pledge registration. In October 2017, the Liaoning High People's Court confirmed in its Civil Judgment (2017) Liao Civil First Instance No. 44 that Minsheng Bank Dalian Branch has a pledge over the pledged property provided by Liu Zhiping and enjoys the right of priority satisfaction. Thus, Liu Zhiping cannot enjoy the right of priority satisfaction over the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company. Fifth, determining that Liu Zhiping enjoys the right of priority satisfaction over the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company would seriously harm the interests of other creditors. On December 24, 2018, the Yichun Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province issued a Civil Ruling (2018) Hei 07 Po 1-5, approving the reorganization plan for Xigang Company and 39 other companies. With the support and cooperation of the majority of creditors, Xigang Company has entered the implementation period of the reorganization plan. The 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company is the bankruptcy property to be distributed in the second phase under the reorganization plan. At this point, recognizing the priority satisfaction right of Mincheng Company's highly disputed transfer-for-security would inevitably provoke dissatisfaction among other creditors, easily trigger social conflicts, and adversely affect the bankruptcy reorganization of Xigang Company and the 39 other companies. In summary, the appeal reasons put forward by Mincheng Company are untenable. Item 2 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2017) Hei Civil First Instance No. 154 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court is correct and should be upheld.

Xigang Company appealed to this Court, requesting: (1) to set aside Item 1 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2017) Hei Min Chu No. 154 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court; (2) to amend the judgment in accordance with the law to confirm that Xigang Company bears principal and interest of RMB 250 million in loans to Mincheng Company, or to remand for retrial; and (3) to have Mincheng Company bear the court acceptance fees for the first and second instances and the property preservation fees. Facts and Reasons: (I) The first-instance judgment erred in finding that the principal amount of the creditor's right that Mincheng Company holds against Xigang Company is RMB 1,059,244,471.52, based on the Loan Contract, the Debt Settlement Agreement, the Agreement, and the Supplementary Agreement. First, the principal amount of loans borrowed by Xigang Company from Mincheng Company is only RMB 250 million. The loans received by Xigang Company from Mincheng Company and its platform companies are only: (a) RMB 100 million transferred from Tangyuan County Mingqi Mineral Products Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mingqi Company) into Xigang Company's account on June 25, 2013; (b) RMB 100 million transferred from Mincheng Company into Xigang Company's account on July 25, 2013; and (c) RMB 50 million transferred from Mincheng Company into Xigang Company's account on February 11, 2014, totaling RMB 250 million. No loan contract was signed between the parties at the time of these three loans. The other loans identified in the first-instance judgment all occurred between Mincheng Company, Harbin Minlong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Minlong Company) and Xilin Iron and Steel Group Acheng Iron and Steel Co., Ltd., Xigang Group Denghai Mining Co., Ltd., Dalian Aofei Trade Co., Ltd., Dalian Kaiyang Trade Co., Ltd., and Cuihongshan Company (hereinafter respectively referred to as Acheng Company, Denghai Company, Aofei Company, Kaiyang Company, or collectively as the actual borrowers). Although no loan contract was signed between the lenders and the actual borrowers at the time of these loan transactions, the actual borrowers recorded the amounts received as their own external debts in the financial accounts under "other payables." Second, the Loan Contract, the Debt Settlement Agreement, the Agreement, and the Supplementary Agreement were formed by collusion between Xigang Company and Mincheng Company to evade execution by other creditors, and did not reflect the true intent of the parties; they should be held invalid. Xigang Company stated during the second-instance trial that the legal basis for claiming the invalidity of the Loan Contract, Debt Settlement Agreement, Agreement, and Supplementary Agreement is primarily Article 154 of the General Provisions of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Provisions of the Civil Law), which provides that "a civil juristic act performed by a person with a counterparty through malicious collusion that harms the lawful rights and interests of others is null and void," and Item (1) of Article 33 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, which provides that "the following acts relating to the debtor's property are null and void: (1) concealing or transferring property to evade debts," among others. Around mid-2014, the steel market was sluggish, and banks recalled loans, causing Xigang Company's capital chain to break, leaving it unable to repay multiple huge debts. Many courts across the country were preparing to take preservation and enforcement measures against Xigang Company's assets. The equity interests in Cuihongshan Company and Xigang Group Harbin Longjun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longjun Company) constituted the only high-quality assets remaining for Xigang Company. If executed, Xigang Company would completely lose its ability to regenerate. Moreover, Xigang Company's assets included a substantial amount of worker production self-rescue funds; if executed, the workers' investments could not be recovered, posing a significant risk to social stability. For these reasons, in order to preserve Xigang Company's assets and avoid bankruptcy, it was decided through discussions between Xigang Company and Mincheng Company to temporarily transfer the equity interests held by Xigang Company in Cuihongshan Company and Longjun Company to Mincheng Company's name. However, both parties clearly understood that this equity transfer was merely superficial and temporary and did not reflect the true intent of either party. To achieve the purpose of the equity transfer, Xigang Company and Mincheng Company agreed to use a security transfer (rangyu danbao) method. Because the equity values of Longjun Company and Cuihongshan Company were relatively large, while the amount of Mincheng Company's creditor's right against Xigang Company was relatively small (only RMB 250 million), to make the form complete, the parties negotiated to expand the scope and amount of Xigang Company's debts to Mincheng Company. Specifically, through the execution of a debt settlement agreement, Xigang Company assumed the debts of the actual borrowers to Mincheng Company, Minlong Company, etc., totaling RMB 765 million. From that point, Xigang Company's liabilities to Mincheng Company increased from RMB 250 million to RMB 1.015 billion. While increasing the debts through the debt settlement agreement, to prevent objections from other creditors, Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping, designated by Mincheng Company, also signed a series of supplementary Loan Contracts, creating the formal appearance that the Loan Contracts were signed before the transfers, in order to align with the flow of funds. In terms of content, the actual transfers and debt settlements were restructured as instruction transfers from the lender Liu Zhiping to the borrower (Xigang Company). Subsequently, through the execution of the Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement, under the guise of providing security for the above debts, Xigang Company transferred its 64% equity interest in Cuihongshan Company and 100% equity interest in Longjun Company to Liu Zhiping, designated by Mincheng Company, and completed the industrial and commercial registration changes, thereby precluding enforcement of the above Xigang Company assets by other creditors. The execution of these agreements meets the constitutive elements of a false declaration of intent made through collusion. Pursuant to Article 146 of the General Provisions of the Civil Law, which provides that "a civil juristic act performed by a person with a counterparty based on a false declaration of intent is null and void," these agreements should be held invalid. The first-instance judgment found that "since the written contracts in this case are genuine, the declaration of intent is therefore true and effective," equating the intent expressed externally by the declarant with the true inner intent, thereby ignoring the provisions of the Civil Law and the Contract Law concerning situations where the actor's true intent is not reflected when entering into a contract. The first-instance court failed to comprehensively review and evaluate the evidence submitted by Xigang Company that the true intent at the time of contracting the contracts was inconsistent with the content of the written contracts, and improperly denied Xigang Company's applications for evidence investigation and expert evaluation, leading to a fundamental error in fact-finding. Based on the above two points, the actual principal amount of the creditor's right that Mincheng Company holds against Xigang Company is RMB 250 million, not the RMB 1,059,244,471.52 found by the first-instance court. (II) The first-instance judgment erred in characterizing the transfer of Longjun Company's equity as a debt satisfaction (dizhai) act, concluding that such act had been fully performed, and thereby deducting RMB 362,043,732 from Xigang Company's debts. First, the change in Longjun Company's equity was to implement the agreement reached between Xigang Company and Mincheng Company, i.e., to protect Xigang Company's assets and prevent execution by other creditors, not to satisfy debts. Second, the agreement to change Longjun Company's equity was not actually performed. In the first instance, Mincheng Company argued that the assessed value of some of Longjun Company's assets could be directly offset against its debts to Xigang Company, relying on the Agreement dated June 13, 2014, between Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping, and the Supplementary Agreement dated August 13, 2015, between Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping, which provided that Xigang Company would transfer Longjun Company's equity to Liu Zhiping to secure the realization of his creditor's rights. Accordingly, these agreements did not express an intent for debt satisfaction, and neither Mincheng Company nor Liu Zhiping, as designated by Mincheng Company, had any intention to actually hold that equity interest. Therefore, after the execution of these agreements, Mincheng Company did not actually control Longjun Company, and the actual right holder of the 100% equity interest in Longjun Company remained Xigang Company. On May 15, 2017, Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping entered into another Agreement, which did not account for the parties' creditor's rights and debts, nor did it specify the scope or method of debt satisfaction using Longjun Company. Moreover, after execution of the above agreements, the actual handover of Longjun Company was still not completed. Therefore, under circumstances where Xigang Company disputed the actual handover and Mincheng Company failed to provide evidence proving that it had completed the acceptance and control, the first-instance judgment found that "both parties have no objection to the fact that Longjun Company has been actually accepted and controlled by Mincheng Company" and concluded that the debt satisfaction using Longjun Company had been fully performed, lacking factual and legal basis. Third, based on the existing evidence, the equity interest in Longjun Company does not qualify for direct debt satisfaction. (a) Article 1.1 of the Agreement signed in May 2017 provided that the exact amount of Xigang Company's debt to Liu Zhiping shall be determined through reconciliation between the parties. To date, the parties have not confirmed the amount of the creditor's right secured by the transfer (rangyu danbao) of Longjun Company. (b) Article 2.2 of the Agreement signed in May 2017 provided that the value of Longjun Company's assets shall be determined based on the appraisal value issued by an appraisal institution, with a fluctuation of no more than 5%, to be confirmed by both parties through agreement. Accordingly, even though the parties jointly selected Heilongjiang Dongyu Zhenye Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongyu Company) to appraise some of Longjun Company's assets, pursuant to the above provision, the appraised value issued by Dongyu Company is only the basis for the parties to negotiate the debt satisfaction amount; it may serve as the foundation for the debt satisfaction amount but is not the debt satisfaction amount itself. Since the scope of the appraisal covered only some of Longjun Company's assets, but Mincheng Company claimed satisfaction of the full 100% equity interest in Longjun Company, the parties needed further negotiation to determine the specific satisfaction amount and method based on the appraised value issued by the commissioned appraisal. Third, in the Asset Appraisal Report (Hei Dong Ping Bao Zi [2017] No. 30) titled "Asset Appraisal Report on Partial Assets and Liabilities of Harbin Longjun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the Asset Appraisal Report), Dongyu Company listed certain uncertain matters, such as pending issues and legal disputes in the Longjun real estate project, as provisional costs: handling fees for the penalty for exceeding the construction area of 5,783 square meters, temporarily estimated at RMB 51,740,000; and costs for work stoppage claims, temporarily estimated at RMB 51,692,226. These two items totaled over RMB 100 million, deducted directly from the appraised value of Longjun Company as unforeseen expenditure items. Xigang Company argued that the provisional amounts listed in the appraisal report under this item were excessively high and lacked basis. Exhibit 28 submitted by Mincheng Company in the first instance showed that the penalty for exceeding the construction area handled by Longjun Company was only about RMB 900,000, less than 1.8% of the appraised price. This indicates that the appraised value issued by Dongyu Company was indeed problematic. Given that Xigang Company raised objections to Dongyu Company and continued to raise objections during the first-instance trial, the first-instance court failed to examine the matter and instead, on the ground that Xigang Company did not provide relevant response opinions issued by Dongyu Company, concluded that Xigang Company's defense was untenable. This finding is erroneous. Fourth, allowing Mincheng Company to price and satisfy debts with Longjun Company's equity damages the lawful rights and interests of other creditors. On June 11, 2018, the Yichun Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province issued a Civil Ruling (2018) Hei 07 Po Shen Zi No. 1 and a Decision (2018) Hei 07 Po 1-1, declaring that Xigang Company had entered into bankruptcy reorganization proceedings. To preserve its assets, Xigang Company assumed huge debts of the actual borrowers without any consideration and used the 100% equity interest in Longjun Company as security, completing the industrial and commercial registration changes. However, from 2014 to the present, the equity transfer of Longjun Company has not been truly completed, and Xigang Company and Mincheng Company have not reached an agreement on the amount or method of debt satisfaction using Longjun Company. The first-instance finding that the debt satisfaction act had been completed clearly constitutes a satisfaction of an individual debtor, violating the relevant provisions of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law and harming the interests of other creditors. (III) In the first instance, Xigang Company submitted applications for expert evaluation and evidence investigation to the first-instance collegial panel to prove that the Debt Settlement Agreement, Loan Contracts, Agreement, etc., were false declarations of intent made through collusion, but these applications were not granted. First, the Loan Contract is the only evidence Mincheng Company relies on to assert that Xigang Company is the original debtor, but the content of the Loan Contract contradicts the content of the Debt Settlement Agreement. To prove that the Loan Contracts were not signed on the dates indicated or before the transfers occurred, Xigang Company applied for judicial evaluation to determine whether the eight Loan Contracts involved were formed at the same time. However, the court repeatedly deferred the matter, citing "decisions to be made by the collegial panel after deliberation," and failed to respond until the final trial. Xigang Company argues that the Loan Contracts are key evidence in this dispute, and the first-instance court's refusal or failure to respond to a matter that should have been evaluated prevented the clarification of basic facts in this case. Second, Liu Zhiping is a key party in this case, as he acted on behalf of Mincheng Company in colluding with Xigang Company to make false representations. In this case, the Debt Settlement Agreement and Loan Contracts designate Liu Zhiping as the successor of rights; therefore, Liu Zhiping is a party who must appear in court. During the first-instance trial, Xigang Company repeatedly requested that Liu Zhiping appear in person for questioning, but the court ignored these requests. Xigang Company had no choice but to submit an application for evidence investigation to the court, providing an outline of questions, requesting the court to question Liu Zhiping and prepare an interrogation record, but the court still refused to question him. The first-instance court's refusal of Xigang Company's above applications for evidence collection made it impossible for Xigang Company to prove the factual allegations it raised, thereby causing errors in the factual findings of the first-instance judgment. (IV) The proceedings in this case should be suspended pending the outcome of case (2018) Hei 07 Min Chu No. 32 of the Yichun Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province [hereinafter referred to as case (2018) Hei 07 Min Chu No. 32]. In the first instance, Xigang Company entered into bankruptcy proceedings. Under the direction of the bankruptcy administrator, creditor Jiamusi Dongxing Coal Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongxing Company), when declaring and registering its claims, believed that the transactions between Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping and others were clearly improper, involving inflated debts, preferential satisfaction of individual creditors, etc., seriously damaging Dongxing Company's right to fair satisfaction. In September 2018, Dongxing Company filed a lawsuit with the Yichun Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province, naming Xigang Company as the defendant, and Mincheng Company, Denghai Company, Aofei Company, Kaiyang Company, Cuihongshan Company, Minlong Company, Liu Zhiping, Guan Wenji, and Lu Liguo as third parties, requesting the court to revoke the series of Debt Settlement Agreements, Loan Contracts, and the equity security transfer (rangyu danbao) Agreements dated June 13 and June 20, 2014, entered into between Xigang Company and the above third parties, and to confirm that third party Liu Zhiping does not enjoy priority rights to satisfy his claims against the 100% equity interest in Longjun Company and the 64% equity interest in Cuihongshan Company. The Yichun Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province has accepted the case, with case number (2018) Hei 07 Min Chu No. 32. Given that the Loan Contracts and Agreements that third party Dongxing Company seeks to revoke are the sole basis for Mincheng Company's claim against Xigang Company, Xigang Company believes that this case and the above-mentioned case (2018) Hei 07 Min Chu No. 32, which is currently being tried, are factually intertwined. Pursuant to Item (5) of the first paragraph of Article 150 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), since this case should be determined based on the outcome of case (2018) Hei 07 Min Chu No. 32, the proceedings in this case should be suspended. Xigang Company submitted an application for suspension of proceedings in the first instance, but it was not granted. In summary, the first-instance judgment contains errors in fact-finding and evidence investigation, and Xigang Company requests that the second-instance court set aside the first-instance judgment and amend it. After the expiration of the appeal period, this Court received from Xigang Company a new Notice of Appeal sent by mail on February 25, 2019, in which the first appeal request was changed to: "Set aside Item 1 of the Civil Judgment (2017) Hei Min Chu No. 154, and confirm in accordance with the law that the appellant bears principal of RMB 1,059,244,471.52 in loans to the appellee, from which the RMB 465,475,958 for debt satisfaction using Longjun Company shall be deducted." Before this Court received that notice of appeal, Xigang Company telephoned to withdraw it. During the second-instance trial, Xigang Company's authorized agent further proposed to change the appeal requests to: "1. Set aside Item 1 of the Civil Judgment (2017) Hei Min Chu No. 154, and amend the judgment in accordance with the law to confirm that the appellant bears principal and interest of RMB 339,244,471.52 in loans to the appellee. 2. The court acceptance fees for the first and second instances and the property preservation fees shall be borne by the appellee." Minchemg Company argued in its defense that the three grounds of appeal stated by Xigang Company in its appellate brief were all without factual or legal basis and should be dismissed. (I) The amount of principal found at first instance was correct, and the "Loan Contract," "Agreement," "Supplementary Agreement," and the debt-for-asset "Agreement" were all legally valid. First, the construction in progress of Longjun Company and the equity of Cuihongshan Company were both pledged earlier, so there was no possibility of concealing and preserving high-quality assets, fabricating and exaggerating debts, or excluding other creditors from repayment, nor were the secured assets the only remaining assets of Xigang Company. The civil judgment of the Beijing High People's Court (2016) Jing Min Zhong Zi No. 197 (second-instance civil judgment on the financial loan contract dispute between China Export-Import Bank and Xigang Company, et al.) found that on June 20, 2013, Xigang Company mortgaged the core assets of its subsidiary Longjun Company, namely the Xigang Jiayuan real estate construction project and the land use rights, to China Export-Import Bank, signing a "Construction in Progress Mortgage Contract," and the invalidity of the mortgage was not confirmed until the final judgment took effect. According to the "Company Equity Registration Form" for Cuihongshan Company provided by the Market Supervision Administration of Xunke County, Xigang Company held 80% equity in Cuihongshan Company, which had been pledged to the Dalian Branch of Minsheng Bank as early as September 2013. In December 2014, to avoid Xigang Company's bankruptcy, Mincheng Company was again forced to agree to pledge that equity to the Dalian Branch of Minsheng Bank for a loan of RMB 490 million to Xigang Company. On July 7, 2016, Xigang Company transferred its 20% equity (valued at RMB 30 million) in Yichun Beifang Cement Co., Ltd. to Li Zhanjiang. Currently, Xigang Company still holds 63% equity in Dengta Company, with a registered capital of RMB 249 million. In summary, no matter from which point in time or perspective, there was no concealment. Second, "malicious collusion" is an excuse fabricated by Xigang Company to evade debts; it neither accords with the facts nor stands to reason. Given that Mincheng Company's own huge loan claims had no security guarantee whatsoever and Xigang Company had not paid a single cent, Mincheng Company had no reason to harm its own interests by colluding maliciously with Xigang Company to protect Xigang Company's assets. The loans in this case were genuine, the contracts were genuine, the debt guarantees were genuine, and the assertion of malicious collusion and concealment of assets does not hold. Third, the finding that the loan principal was RMB 1.059 billion has ample factual and legal basis. The loan contracts in this case bear the company seal of Xigang Company and the handwritten signature of its legal representative, and the loan contracts are corroborated by bank transfer receipts. Loan contracts are practical contracts, taking effect upon receipt of the loan funds; whether the contract was signed before the loan or supplemented after receipt of the funds does not affect the validity of the loan contract. Xigang Company's request at the first-instance trial to determine the formation dates of the eight loan contracts involved is legally meaningless and is merely a delay tactic. Xigang Company, which bears the burden of proof for its claim of malicious collusion between Mincheng Company and Xigang Company, failed to provide any evidence and must bear the consequences of its failure to prove. According to commercial custom, if the subsidiaries of Xigang Company had not provided any collateral to the creditor Mincheng Company, it would have been impossible for Mincheng Company to lend such a huge amount. Fourth, the content of the "Debt Offset Agreement" does not conflict with the loan agreement. The "Debt Offset Agreement" is a financial processing agreement, a method for handling accounts among the companies, and does not contradict the loan agreement. The "Debt Offset Agreement" was a template document drafted by Xigang Company, containing several typographical errors, but these do not affect the determination of the creditor-debtor relationship. The "Debt Offset Agreement" came first, followed by the "Supplementary Agreements" (2014, 2015) and the "Debt-for-Asset Agreement" (2017). Considering all the evidence in the case, especially the multiple supplementary agreements and the debt-for-asset agreement formed later, it is clearly evident that there is no issue of unclear identification of the creditor or debtor. Regardless of which subsidiary the loans flowed through, they were ultimately transferred to Xigang Company for unified emergency use. Fifth, Xigang Company admitted to the remaining multiple loans during the first-instance trial. Xigang Company already admitted to the RMB 43 million remitted by Liu Zhiping into Xigang Company, as recorded in the first-instance trial transcript. On December 24, 2018, Xigang Company and 40 other companies were adjudicated by the court to undergo consolidated bankruptcy. In the reorganization plan, the bankruptcy administrator pointed out that Xigang Company, Agang Company, and others "exhibited integration in personnel, management, business, property, and fund use, and there were high amounts of related debts and mutual guarantees among them." Accordingly, the loan of RMB 45 million remitted to Agang Company should be repaid by Xigang Company. From the remittance slips in the supplementary evidence submitted by Xigang Company at first instance, it can be seen that on the day Ore Company and Kaiyang Company received loans of over RMB 100 million, they immediately remitted the funds into the account of Dengta Company. Xigang Company held 63% equity in Dengta Company through Shenzhen Rui'anda Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Rui'anda Company), making it the actual controller. During the first-instance trial, Xigang Company provided the original financial accounts of Dengta Company as evidence, which conversely proved that Xigang Company was the actual controller of Rui'anda Company. Accordingly, it is for Xigang Company to explain where the RMB 230 million transferred to Dengta Company was used. The RMB 650,000 remitted on April 14, 2016, was evidenced by an IOU from Xigang Company's senior executive Liu Wenbo. The subsequently signed "Supplementary Agreement" confirmed that Xigang Company would bear this amount. The loan details of Cuihongshan Company provided by Xigang Company at first instance recorded that the RMB 140 million involving Lu Liguo and Guan Wenji was "group loan booked to Cuihongshan," indicating that this sum was actually controlled by Xigang Company. The loan details of Dengta Company indicated "group company loan booked to Dengta Company" and "group company loan booked to Ore Company." In its first-instance reply, Xigang Company argued that the interest on the RMB 140 million loan should be 10%, not 14.3%, without denying the existence of the creditor-debtor relationship. Sixth, Liu Zhiping is not a party whose presence is mandatory at trial, and his failure to appear personally does not affect the determination of facts or the substantive handling of the case. Liu Zhiping appeared personally at the first two sessions of the first-instance trial; although he did not appear at the latter two sessions, he had authorized lawyers to participate in the litigation, and he also submitted a written defense signed by himself to the court. During the second-instance trial, Mincheng Company's authorized agent argued in supplementary defense: "After the conclusion of the first two trial sessions, Xigang Company sent its own personnel to Liu Zhiping's home under the guise of serving a summons to harass him. Liu Zhiping dared not continue to appear in court and instead authorized a lawyer to appear on his behalf. This case is not one concerning personal status; Liu Zhiping had already made statements regarding all facts of the case during the first two appearances, submitted a written defense, and also authorized a lawyer to appear in court on his behalf." (II) The datio in solutum by Longjun Company had been completed and was legally valid. The dispute in this case concerning Longjun Company was no longer about the validity of the transfer-for-security arrangement, but rather about the validity of the datio in solutum. First, the court should recognize the validity of the debt-for-asset "Agreement" signed by the parties. Clause 3.1 of the debt-for-asset "Agreement" signed by Xigang Company, Liu Zhiping, and Longjun Company stipulated: "Upon the entry into effect of this Agreement, Party A shall transfer 100% equity of Longjun Company to Party B, and the corresponding amount of claims held by Party B shall be offset." The parties had the intention to extinguish the old debt. Second, the debt settlement through Longjun Company's equity had been completed. Xigang Company admitted during the first-instance trial that Longjun Company was actually controlled by Mincheng Company. Within a few days of signing the agreement, the construction in progress was actually handed over; within ten days, construction teams entered the site to begin work. All types of approval procedures, construction procurement contracts, construction drawings, and archives and company seals were handed over on the spot on the day of signing, as evidenced by a handover list signed and sealed by both parties. At this point, the datio in solutum was completed, far more than one year before Xigang Company's bankruptcy, and thus did not violate the provisions of the Bankruptcy Law. Third, the "Asset Appraisal Report" is valid. Dongyu Company was the appraisal agency selected by Xigang Company and possessed the relevant qualifications. All parties jointly signed the "Asset Appraisal Engagement Letter," and Dongyu Company appraised in accordance with the scope of commissioned appraisal stipulated in the letter. In response to the objections raised by Xigang Company in its first-instance submission titled "Letter of Objection to the Appraisal Result of Longjun Company's Real Estate," Mincheng Company argued that "the matter can be dealt with separately through settlement based on the actual situation, but this cannot negate the validity of the appraisal report. Mincheng Company is also willing to settle accounts with Xigang Company based on the actual situation after handling the claims for work stoppage and the procedures for the built area exceeding the approved construction area." (III) The first-instance procedure was lawful. There were not just one but two related cases filed by the third party Dongxing Company in separate proceedings. After Dongxing Company filed its first lawsuit, the Xilin District People's Court of Yichun City accepted the case but did not try it, delaying for seven months; thereafter, Dongxing Company withdrew the lawsuit. In September 2018, Dongxing Company again sued on the same grounds before the Yichun Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province; similarly, the accepting court accepted the case but did not try it, and service of process had not yet been completed. The filing dates of these cases were later than the filing date of this case, and the causes of action were different; thus, they should not serve as grounds for suspending this case.

Minchemg Company initiated the lawsuit at the court of first instance, requesting: that Xigang Company repay the loan principal of RMB 1,059,244,471.52 and interest (from May 9, 2013, to November 15, 2017, amounting to RMB 951,071,798.34, and calculated up to the date of actual payment); that Mincheng Company be entitled to priority in repayment from the proceeds of discounting, auctioning, or selling the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company held by Liu Zhiping; and that Xigang Company bear the litigation costs, appraisal fees, and other expenses of this case.

Facts and Reasons: Xigang Company, in its own name or that of its subsidiaries, borrowed funds multiple times from Mincheng Company for production operations and short-term bank loan rollovers. The total loan principal currently amounts to RMB 1,059,244,471.52, with accumulated interest of RMB 1,333,070,602.41. On June 16 and June 26, 2014, Xigang Company transferred its 100% equity in Longjun Company and 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company as transfer-for-security to the name of Liu Zhiping, the third party designated by Mincheng Company. At the same time, Mincheng Company and Liu Zhiping entered into an equity proxy holding agreement. In early 2017, the parties agreed to use Longjun Company's assets to offset interest on the debt amounting to RMB 362,043,732.00. Thereafter, Xigang Company failed to repay the remaining outstanding debt as agreed.

Xigang Company argued in its defense: First, this case should be suspended. Dongxing Company, with Xigang Company as the defendant and Cuihongshan Company, Minlong Company, Liu Zhiping, Guan Wenji, Lu Liguo, et al. as third parties, filed a lawsuit in the Xilin District People's Court of Yichun City, seeking to revoke a series of "Debt Offset Agreements," "Loan Contracts," and "Agreements" signed between Xigang Company and the third party Liu Zhiping. Since these agreements are the basis on which Mincheng Company asserts claims against Xigang Company and claims priority in repayment, if these agreements are ultimately revoked, it would directly affect the outcome of this case. Therefore, this case should be suspended. Second, Mincheng Company is not a proper plaintiff. The lender under the "Loan Contracts" involved was Liu Zhiping, and the loan method involved Liu Zhiping remitting loan funds into the accounts of Xigang Company or its subsidiaries through the account of Mincheng Company or other company accounts. Mincheng Company is not the lender in the loan legal relationship, and not all of the loan amounts involved were paid by Mincheng Company or received by Xigang Company. Although in June 2014, Mincheng Company and Xigang Company signed several "Debt Offset Agreements" to change the creditor to Mincheng Company and the debtor to Xigang Company through assignment of claims and assumption of debts, the "Debt Offset Agreement" signed by the three parties on June 14, 2014, stipulated the assignment of all of Mincheng Company's claims to Liu Zhiping. Thus, Mincheng Company had lost its creditor status and had no right to claim repayment from Xigang Company. There was no agency relationship between Mincheng Company and Liu Zhiping. Mincheng Company had assigned the claims to Liu Zhiping and could not prove that Liu Zhiping held the claims on behalf of Mincheng Company. Its assertion that it directed Liu Zhiping to sign the "Loan Contracts" and handle the equity transfer lacks factual basis. Third, the "Loan Contracts," "Debt Offset Agreements," and "Agreements" involved do not reflect the true intentions of the parties. Due to the downturn in the steel market, Xigang Company and its affiliated enterprises borrowed funds from Minlong Company, Liu Zhiping, et al. To ensure the interests of Mincheng Company and others and to preserve Xigang Company's assets, the parties decided to transfer the equity in Cuihongshan Company and Longjun Company in the form of transfer-for-security to Liu Zhiping's name nominally, thereby preventing other creditors from enforcing against Xigang Company's assets, and subsequently signed a series of "Loan Contracts," "Debt Offset Agreements," and "Agreements" retroactively. Fourth, the "Asset Appraisal Report" cannot serve as the basis for Xigang Company's debt settlement to Liu Zhiping using Longjun Company's assets. Xigang Company has sent a letter to Dongyu Company raising objections to the "Asset Appraisal Report." To date, Xigang Company has not received a reply from Dongyu Company regarding the objections. Therefore, the "Asset Appraisal Report" cannot be used as the basis for Xigang Company's settlement of debts owed to Liu Zhiping. Fifth, the interest on the loan claimed by Mincheng Company exceeds the agreed amount and should not be upheld. The "Tender Notice" of Cuihongshan Company and the "Receipts" issued to Guan Wenji and Lu Liguo both indicate that the interest on this financing was 10% per annum, not 14.3% or 23.5%. The amount set off in the "Debt Offset Agreement" involved was RMB 875 million, with interest calculated at 18% per annum, not 23.5%. Sixth, the nature of the "Agreement" signed between Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping regarding Cuihongshan Company is transfer-for-security, which cannot produce the effect of security under property law, and this "Agreement" harms the interests of other creditors. Xigang Company has filed a lawsuit with the Xunke County People's Court of Heilongjiang Province, seeking confirmation that the transfer of Cuihongshan Company's equity between Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping is invalid. Therefore, Mincheng Company does not enjoy priority in repayment with respect to the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company.

During the trial of first instance, Liu Zhiping confirmed that the actual right holders of the loans involved were Mincheng Company, and that Mincheng Company had the right to assert claims against Xigang Company.

The court of first instance held that the Loan Contracts, Debt Assignment Agreements, Agreements, and Supplementary Agreements involved were all true expressions of intent of the parties, their contents did not violate the mandatory prohibitive provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and there were no statutory circumstances rendering them void, and therefore they should be recognized as legally valid. Although Xigang Company argued that it and Mincheng Company had signed the series of agreements involved by inflating Xigang Company's debts in order to transfer Xigang Company's high-quality assets, and that these agreements were not the true expressions of intent of the parties, Xigang Company did not provide evidence to support this claim. Although Xigang Company applied for an appraisal of the time of formation of the official seals on the Loan Contracts involved, even if such an appraisal were conducted, it would not prove that the agreements involved were not the true expressions of intent of the parties. The court of first instance did not support Xigang Company's defense.

(1) Whether Mincheng Company in this case has the right to assert claims. Although Liu Zhiping was one of the signing parties to the series of Loan Contracts, Agreements, and Supplementary Agreements involved, Liu Zhiping confirmed during the trial that the actual right holders of the loans in this case were Mincheng Company, and that Mincheng Company had the right to assert claims against Xigang Company. Moreover, some of the funds in this case were also paid by Mincheng Company. Therefore, Mincheng Company in this case has the right to assert claims as a plaintiff.

(2) How to determine the amount of loan principal and interest involved in the case. During the period from May 7, 2013, to June 11, 2014, Liu Zhiping and Xigang Company entered into eight Loan Contracts, which stipulated a loan amount of 875 million yuan. Mincheng Company also provided bank transfer formalities for the payment of the said 875 million yuan in accordance with the provisions of the foregoing Loan Contracts. On April 9 and 11, 2014, Guan Wenji and Lu Liguo jointly lent 140 million yuan to Cuihongshan Company. On June 20, Guan Wenji and Lu Liguo respectively entered into Agreements with Cuihongshan Company and Liu Zhiping, transferring the creditor's rights of 140 million yuan to Liu Zhiping. Xigang Company also issued the Group Loan Schedule and the Xilin Iron and Steel Group Co., Ltd. Loan Interest Calculation Table to confirm the aforesaid loans. Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping entered into an Agreement and a Supplemental Agreement on June 20, 2014, and August 13, 2015, respectively, reconfirming the aforesaid loans. On April 20, 2016, Longjun Company borrowed 650,000 yuan from Liu Zhiping. Subsequently, Liu Zhiping and Xigang Company entered into an agreement, confirming that the 650,000 yuan was a debt of Xigang Company. On June 16, 2014, Liu Zhiping remitted 43,594,471.52 yuan to Xigang Company in nine separate transactions. Xigang Company agreed at trial to repay this amount to Liu Zhiping, and Liu Zhiping agreed that Mincheng Company could claim this amount from Xigang Company. Based on the foregoing facts, the court of first instance determined the loan principal in this case to be 1,059,244,471.52 yuan (875 million + 140 million + 650,000 + 43,594,471.52). Because Xigang Company failed to repay the said loan principal as agreed, constituting a breach of contract, Mincheng Company's claim that Xigang Company should repay the loan principal and interest to it should be supported.

All eight Loan Contracts in this case stipulated an interest rate of 23.5% before tax per annum and 18% after tax per annum, with the tax burden to be borne by Xigang Company, and Liu Zhiping to receive interest at the after-tax annual rate of 18%. Moreover, the Intermediate People's Court of Yichun City, Heilongjiang Province, accepted Xigang Company's restructuring application on June 11, 2018. Pursuant to Article 46 of the Bankruptcy Law, the accrual of interest on interest-bearing claims shall cease from the date of acceptance of the bankruptcy petition. Therefore, Xigang Company should pay Mincheng Company interest for the period from the actual date of disbursement of the loans (with the base amounts and dates: for 45 million yuan, from May 9, 2013; for 100 million yuan, from June 25, 2013; for 100 million yuan, from July 25, 2013; for 250 million yuan, from December 11, 2013; for 100 million yuan, from December 12, 2013; for 30 million yuan, from January 29, 2014; for 50 million yuan, from February 11, 2014; for 100 million yuan, from May 12, 2014; for 100 million yuan, from June 13, 2014), up to June 11, 2018, at the after-tax annual rate of 18%. On June 20, 2014, the Agreements respectively entered into by Guan Wenji and Lu Liguo with Cuihongshan Company and Liu Zhiping, as well as the Group Loan Schedule and the Loan Interest Calculation Table issued by Xigang Company, all reflected that the interest rate on the 140 million yuan loan of Guan Wenji and Lu Liguo involved in this case was 10% per annum. Meanwhile, the Supplemental Agreement dated August 13, 2015, in this case stipulated that if the repayment period exceeded six months, the interest would be calculated at the after-tax annual rate of 18%. Therefore, Xigang Company should pay interest to Mincheng Company in accordance with the aforesaid agreement (with the bases: for 130 million yuan, from April 9, 2014, to August 13, 2015, calculated at 10% per annum; for 10 million yuan, from April 11, 2014, to August 13, 2015, calculated at 10% per annum; for 140 million yuan, from August 14, 2015, to June 11, 2018, calculated at the after-tax annual rate of 18%). On June 16, 2014, Liu Zhiping remitted 43,594,471.52 yuan to Xigang Company in nine separate transactions. On August 13, 2015, the Supplemental Agreement signed by both parties confirmed the outstanding loan principal and interest at the after-tax annual rate of 18%. Therefore, Xigang Company should pay Mincheng Company interest for the period from June 16, 2014, to June 11, 2018, based on 43,594,471.52 yuan, at the after-tax annual rate of 18%. Since no interest was agreed upon for the 650,000 yuan loan in this case, Xigang Company should pay interest for the period from June 19, 2017 (the date of filing the lawsuit) to June 11, 2018, at the standard of the contemporaneous comparable loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China. In this case, the Agreement dated June 13, 2014, and the Supplemental Agreement dated August 13, 2015, both stipulated that Xigang Company would transfer the equity of Longjun Company to Liu Zhiping to secure the realization of his creditor's rights. Subsequently, both parties agreed to use the equity and assets of Longjun Company to satisfy the debt, with the value to be determined based on the appraisal value issued by an asset appraisal institution jointly selected by both parties. On October 18, 2017, Dongyu Company, commissioned by both parties, issued the Asset Appraisal Report, confirming that the appraised value of the company's assets as of April 30, 2017, was 362,043,732 yuan. Moreover, both parties had no objection to the fact that Longjun Company had been actually taken over by Mincheng Company, meaning that the debt satisfaction action had been actually completed. Therefore, the amount of 362,043,732 yuan should be deducted from the outstanding loan principal and interest of Xigang Company. Although Xigang Company argued that the assets of Longjun Company in Xilin District, Yichun City, were not included in the appraisal scope, the agreement signed by both parties expressly stipulated that all assets of Longjun Company under the name in Xilin District, Yichun City, would not be included in this appraisal scope, and the creditor's rights and debts would be borne by Xigang Company. Xigang Company further argued that it had raised objections to Dongyu Company regarding the appraisal report, but it did not provide the relevant reply opinions issued by Dongyu Company. Therefore, the aforesaid defenses of Xigang Company cannot be sustained.

(3) Whether Mincheng Company has the right to claim priority satisfaction from the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company. The Loan Contracts in this case all stipulated that the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company would be used as security. The Agreement dated June 13, 2014, and the Supplemental Agreement dated August 13, 2015, also stipulated that the realization of Liu Zhiping's creditor's rights would be secured in the form of equity transfer, and Liu Zhiping had no intention to actually hold that portion of the equity. It can thus be confirmed that the true purpose of signing these contracts between the parties was not to actually effectuate an equity transfer, but to provide security for the debts involved in the case. However, under the principles of numerus clausus of property rights and the requirement of publicity for property rights, such arrangements have no real right effect nor do they have effect against third parties. At the same time, because Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping did not have a genuine intention to transfer the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company, the actual right holder of the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company remains Xigang Company. Since the Intermediate People's Court of Yichun City, Heilongjiang Province, had already accepted Xigang Company's restructuring application on June 11, 2018, if Mincheng Company were to obtain priority satisfaction from the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company, it would be considered a debt satisfaction to an individual creditor, violating Article 16 of the Bankruptcy Law, which provides that "after the People's Court accepts a bankruptcy petition, any debt satisfaction by the debtor to an individual creditor is void." Therefore, the court of first instance did not support Mincheng Company's claim for priority satisfaction from the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company.

In addition, although Xigang Company and Dongxing Company separately filed other lawsuits with the Xunke County People's Court of Heilongjiang Province and the Intermediate People's Court of Yichun City, Heilongjiang Province, the trial of this case does not depend on the outcome of those other cases and does not fall under the circumstances for suspension of proceedings as stipulated in Article 150 of the Civil Procedure Law. Therefore, Xigang Company's claim that this case should be suspended cannot be sustained.
