This Court is of the opinion that the issues in dispute in this case are: (1) The amount of the loan principal lent by Mincheng Company to Xigang Company and the standard for calculating interest. (2) Whether the agreement between Xigang Company and Mincheng Company to transfer the equity of Longjun Company at a price to offset the debt owed to Mincheng Company is valid; whether the equity agreed to be transferred meets the conditions for debt satisfaction; whether the appraisal report made by a third party on the equity agreed to be transferred can be admitted; whether the agreement has been actually performed. (3) The nature and validity of the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company held by Liu Zhiping, and whether Mincheng Company has the right to priority satisfaction from that equity; whether the court of first instance correctly applied Article 16 of the Bankruptcy Law in dismissing Mincheng Company's claim for priority satisfaction from the proceeds of the shares held by Liu Zhiping. (4) Whether the first-instance procedures were lawful, including: whether the court of first instance's refusal to allow Xigang Company's application for a document examination to determine whether the eight loan contracts involved were executed at the same time violated statutory procedures; whether the court of first instance's failure to question Liu Zhiping according to the outline submitted by Xigang Company and the fact that Liu Zhiping was not present in person during part of the trial rendered the proceedings unlawful; whether the court of first instance should have ordered a suspension of the proceedings in this case pending the outcome of the judgment in case (2018) Hei 07 Min Chu No. 32.

In this second instance, the Court summarized the allegations and defenses of the parties at various litigation stages, including the court session on February 26, 2019, and determined that the parties had no dispute over the following facts of the case:

First, Xigang Company acknowledged that the amount of loan principal due to Mincheng Company was RMB 339,244,471.52, specifically composed of: on June 25, 2013, RMB 100 million remitted by Mingqi Company to the account of Xigang Company; on July 25, 2013, RMB 100 million remitted by Mincheng Company to the account of Xigang Company; on February 11, 2014, RMB 50 million remitted by Mincheng Company to the account of Xigang Company; on May 7, 2013, RMB 45 million remitted by Mincheng Company to the account of Agang Company; on June 16, 2014, RMB 43,594,471.52 remitted by Liu Zhiping in nine installments to the account of Xigang Company; and on April 20, 2016, RMB 650,000 remitted by Mincheng Company to the account of Liu Wenbo, the then legal representative of Longjun Company, for the payment of attorney fees and other business expenses of Longjun Company. The aforesaid loan principal of RMB 339,244,471.52 should be repaid by Xigang Company.

Second, the judgment of first instance found that the amount of loan principal borrowed by Xigang Company from Mincheng Company was RMB 1,059,244,471.52. As above, Mincheng Company and Xigang Company had no dispute over RMB 339,244,471.52 thereof; regarding the remaining amount (RMB 1,059,244,471.52 minus RMB 339,244,471.52), there was no objection to the fact that these funds had been remitted to the relevant accounts of the relevant companies.

Third, regarding the assessed value of Longjun Company, Mincheng Company indicated its agreement to adjustments, specifically as follows: on the basis of RMB 362,043,732 assessed in the "Asset Appraisal Report," add RMB 51,740,000 in fees for handling penalties for the construction of an extra 5,783 square meters, which had been deducted in advance at the time of appraisal, and RMB 51,692,226 in claims for work suspension costs, while simultaneously deducting the RMB 934,240 in administrative penalties that had already been paid; if new fees for penalties for exceeding the construction area, work suspension claims, or other costs arise, they shall be settled separately based on actual circumstances, and creditors, debtors, and others shall have the right to file lawsuits in this regard. Xigang Company raised no objection to the above adjustments. After adjustment, the value of Longjun Company was RMB 464,541,718 (362,043,732 + 51,740,000 + 51,692,226 - 934,240).

Fourth, during the court session of the second instance, both Xigang Company and Mincheng Company confirmed that the "Debt Write-off Agreement" entered into on June 4, 2014, by Xigang Company, Agang Company, and Mincheng Company contained a clerical error, and the actual intention was that Xigang Company would assume the RMB 45 million debt of Agang Company; the agreement entered into on June 4, 2014, among Guan Wenji, Cuihongshan Company, Xigang Company, and Liu Zhiping contained a clerical error, and the actual intention was that Guan Wenji would transfer the creditor's rights to Liu Zhiping, and Cuihongshan Company would transfer the debt to Xigang Company.

The Court holds that the nature of the legal relationship in dispute in this case is a private lending contract dispute. The main contents of the eight "Loan Contracts" involved in the case concern the principal amount, interest rate, loan term, etc., of private lending, with Xigang Company as the borrower and Liu Zhiping as the lender. Article 1, paragraph 1 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases" (hereinafter referred to as the "Private Lending Provisions") stipulates that the term "private lending" as used in these Provisions refers to the conduct of financing among natural persons, legal persons, and other organizations; Article 11 stipulates that for private lending contracts entered into between legal persons, between other organizations, or between them and each other for the needs of production and operation, unless there are circumstances stipulated in Article 52 of the Contract Law or Article 14 of these Provisions, if the parties assert that the private lending contract is valid, the people's court shall support such assertion; Article 14 stipulates that under any of the following circumstances, the people's court shall find the private lending contract invalid: (1) obtaining credit funds from financial institutions and then on-lending them to the borrower at a high interest rate, and the borrower knew or should have known of this in advance; (2) obtaining funds by borrowing from other enterprises or by raising funds from the entity's own employees and then on-lending them to the borrower for profit, and the borrower knew or should have known of this in advance; (3) the lender knew or should have known in advance that the borrower would use the loan for illegal or criminal activities but still provided the loan; (4) violating public order and good customs; (5) other circumstances that violate mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations on validity. According to the above judicial interpretation, the contents stipulated in the eight "Loan Contracts" involved in this case are legal and valid. The "Debt Write-off Agreement" involved in the case and the "Agreements" entered into in June 2014 by Guan Wenji and Lu Liguo respectively with Cuihongshan Company and Liu Zhiping, which stipulate the assignment of creditor's rights and assumption of debts, should also be found valid. The judgment of first instance correctly found the above contracts to be legal and valid, and this Court affirms that finding.

1. The amount of loan principal lent by Mincheng Company to Xigang Company and the standard for calculating interest

With respect to the loans involved in the case, Mincheng Company submitted the "Loan Contracts," "Account Statements," "Debt Write-off Agreement," "Agreements," "IOUs," "Supplement Agreement," and bank customer special receipts, bank debit notices, bank transaction details, "Project Tender Announcement," "Receipts," "Xunke County Cuihongshan Mining Co., Ltd. Loan Schedule," "Loan Interest Calculation Table," "Group Loan Schedule," "Xilin Steel Group Co., Ltd. Loan Interest Calculation Table," "Xigang Group Lighthouse Mining Co., Ltd. Loan Schedule," and other loan contracts, debt instruments, account reconciliation records, and similar contractual documents to prove that the loans agreed in the contracts were paid in place, and that the corresponding amounts were received in the accounts of Xigang Company or its designated companies. Xigang Company did not object to the fact that the corresponding funds flowed into the accounts of Xigang Company or the relevant accounts of other relevant companies, but it only acknowledged its obligation to repay the aforementioned total loan principal of RMB 339,244,471.52 and the interest thereon. The Court holds that, apart from the above undisputed loan principal, although other loan principal was not directly remitted to the account of Xigang Company, it was remitted to the accounts of relevant companies designated by Xigang Company in accordance with the relevant "Loan Contracts." In the loan contracts of this case, the signing and performance took various forms, including: making payment of the loan first and then signing the contract to confirm; after making or receiving payment in the name of a related company, confirming the true creditor or true debtor through an agreement on assignment of creditor's rights or assumption of debts; and conducting reconciliation of the principal and interest of multiple loans occurring over a certain period, listing detailed amounts of principal and interest for several loans, and making arrangements for renewal or repayment. These forms are consistent with the characteristics of signing and performance in private lending, represent a common transaction model in judicial practice, and are also an industry feature distinguishing private lending from financial lending. Through reconciliation between the lender and the borrower, the main contractual terms of the private lending contract, such as the loan amount, interest rate, loan term, and security, were essentially clear. Through forms such as entering into agreements on assignment of creditor's rights and assumption of debts with persons not involved in the case, the creditors and debtors transferred the creditor's rights and debts involved in this case to the names of Liu Zhiping and Xigang Company, respectively. During the first and second instance proceedings, Liu Zhiping consistently confirmed that Mincheng Company was the true creditor and that Mincheng Company would exercise the creditor's rights. Accordingly, from the perspectives of both signing and performance, the private lending contract in this case was formed, became effective, and was fully and actually performed. Mincheng Company actually paid the funds under the loan contract to Xigang Company, and Xigang Company has so far failed to repay most of the loan principal and interest in accordance with the contract, which constitutes a material breach of contract. Xigang Company's refusal to assume the repayment obligation on the ground that the loan funds other than the aforementioned undisputed principal were not directly remitted to the account of Xigang Company lacks legal basis and is inconsistent with the facts; this Court does not support it. Xigang Company should, in accordance with the principle of good faith, perform the contents stipulated in the series of loan contracts and assume the obligation to repay all of the above loan principal and interest. The judgment of first instance found that the amount of loan principal in this case was RMB 1,059,244,471.52 and that Xigang Company should bear the responsibility for repaying the above loan principal and interest; this finding was appropriate, and this Court affirms it.

Xigang Company appealed, arguing that when the above loans were made, the parties to the private lending had not yet signed contracts, and the actual signing dates of the eight "Loan Contracts" involved in the case were not the dates indicated thereon, nor were they signed before the remittances, but were uniformly supplemented later; the true intention of Xigang Company, Mincheng Company, and Liu Zhiping in signing the "Debt Write-off Agreement" and the "Agreements" was to enable Xigang Company to evade debts, which meets the constitutive elements of a false declaration of intent made in collusion, and does not represent the true expression of intent of the parties to the contract; therefore, according to Article 146 of the "General Provisions of the Civil Law," the loan contracts should be invalid. The Court holds that, as above, the loans under the private lending contract had been remitted to the account of the borrower or its designee, and the contract had been fully and actually performed. After the dispute in this case was litigated, the borrower, in the form of self-confessed illegality, interpreted this normal private lending as an illegal act carried out by the borrower and the lender through a false declaration of intent made in collusion, aiming to circumvent the court's compulsory execution of Xigang Company's only remaining high-quality assets to evade debts; the borrower filed another lawsuit seeking confirmation that the equity in Cuihongshan Company belonged to it, and a person not involved in the case twice filed another lawsuit with the same claim to seek confirmation of the invalidity of the loan contract; the borrower relied on this to argue for a suspension of the proceedings in this case; the borrower also raised other grounds to request a postponement of the trial in this case; and the borrower made several inconsistent statements regarding the amount of loan funds received. After the litigation, the above litigation conduct of Xigang Company was inconsistent with the basic principle of good faith litigation. This Court does not support Xigang Company's above claim regarding the invalidity of the contracts.

In the second instance, Mincheng Company argued that Xigang Company was no longer able to pay taxes; that Mincheng Company, as the taxpayer, had the right to seek recourse from the counterparty after paying the taxes first; and that, given Xigang Company's bankruptcy, Mincheng Company could no longer seek recourse, requesting that the second instance amend the judgment to calculate interest on the loan of RMB 875 million at a pre-tax annual rate of 23.5% in installments, increasing the interest amount by RMB 216,967,465.75. The Court holds that the interest rate stipulated in the series of loan contracts in this case is primarily a pre-tax annual rate of 23.5% (including business tax at 5%, city maintenance and construction tax at 7%, education surcharge at 5%, and enterprise income tax at 25%), which is the same interest calculation standard as the post-tax annual rate of 18%; however, the contract stipulates that the borrower shall withhold and remit the taxes, not that the lender shall pay the taxes itself; the business risk inherent in the agreement on withholding and remittance by the borrower should be borne by the borrower in accordance with the contract. When the risk that the loan principal and interest cannot be repaid arises, Mincheng Company's request to change the method of withholding and remitting the taxes included in the interest stipulated in the contract, in an attempt to mitigate or eliminate the business risk, lacks contractual basis. The standard interest rate determined in the first instance for the above loan contracts, i.e., the pre-tax annual rate of 18%, is consistent with the contract and with the facts of this case, and this Court affirms it.

2. Whether the transfer of equity in Longjun Company was a transfer of property in satisfaction of a debt and whether it has been fully performed

On June 13, 2014, Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping entered into the "Agreement," which stipulated that Longjun Company had borrowed RMB 447,159,452.22 from Liu Zhiping and was unable to repay; on June 16, 2014, the parties completed the procedures for the change of equity transfer. Xigang Company transferred 100% of the equity it held in Longjun Company (including the engineering project and creditor's rights and debts) to Liu Zhiping, with the transfer price determined as the net book value of Longjun Company as of the end of May 2014 of RMB 43,594,471.52. On June 16, Liu Zhiping remitted RMB 43,594,471.52 to Xigang Company in nine installments. On August 13, 2015, Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping entered into the "Supplement Agreement," which stipulated: "Party A and Party B entered into an agreement on June 13, 2014, whereby Party A temporarily transferred 100% of the equity it holds in Xigang Group Harbin Longjun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longjun Company) to Party B, to ensure the safety and realization of Party B's creditor's rights. Given that Xigang is currently unable to repay its debts to Party B, in order to ensure that Party B can recover funds as soon as possible, after negotiation, Party A and Party B have reached consensus and entered into this supplement agreement. 1. Party A confirms that, as of June 20, 2015, the principal and interest borrowed from Party B amount to RMB 447,159,452.22, and the payment received from Party B for the temporary transfer of 100% of the equity in Longjun Company is RMB 43,594,471.52, totaling RMB 490,753,923.74. If the principal and interest are repaid within 6 months from June 21, 2015, interest shall be paid at a post-tax annual rate of 12%; for the portion of the repayment period exceeding 6 months, interest shall be paid at a post-tax annual rate of 18%. Interest shall be settled annually. ... 8. If Party A cannot sell the properties to repay the loan to Party B within one year, an intermediary institution shall assess the realizable assets of Longjun Company. Party A shall sell the properties to repay Party B's loan at a price not less than 5% below the assessed value, with the surplus belonging to Party A. The assessed value and range shall not include all taxes and fees arising from the sale of the properties and the properties and parking spaces for the collective housing construction stipulated in Article 7 of this Agreement."

The Court holds that, in the foregoing provisions, the statements such as "temporarily transfer 100% of the equity in Longjun Company to Party B, to ensure the safety and realization of Party B's creditor's rights" and "given that Xigang is currently unable to repay its debts to Party B, in order to ensure that Party B can recover funds as soon as possible" clearly and unambiguously express the intention to secure the realization of the creditor's rights. The creditor and debtor agreed to secure the loan safety through the form of a temporary transfer of 100% of the equity in Longjun Company. It was also stipulated that "if Party A cannot sell the properties to repay the loan to Party B within one year, an intermediary institution shall assess the realizable assets of Longjun Company. Party A shall sell the properties to repay Party B's loan at a price not less than 5% below the assessed value, with the surplus belonging to Party A." This stipulation makes clear that "if Party A cannot sell the properties to repay the loan to Party B within one year" means that, although 100% of the equity in Longjun Company had already been transferred to the name of Liu Zhiping, Xigang Company still had the right to sell the real estate under Longjun Company to offset the specific debts owed to Liu Zhiping as agreed. The Court holds that the essential content of the above provisions in the "Agreement" and the "Supplement Agreement" is to secure the realization of the aforementioned creditor's rights by transferring 100% of the equity in Longjun Company to the name of Liu Zhiping, while Xigang Company retained shareholder rights such as major decision-making powers over Longjun Company; after the debt was fully performed, 100% of the equity in Longjun Company would revert to Xigang Company; if the debt could not be repaid as agreed, the creditor could offset the debt against the assessed asset value of Longjun Company. This is consistent with the legal characteristics of alienation guarantee. As an atypical security widely used in civil and commercial activities, it does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations on validity, and the aforementioned "Agreement" and "Supplement Agreement" should be found valid.

On May 15, 2017, Xigang Company as Party A, Liu Zhiping as Party B, and Longjun Company as Party C entered into another agreement stipulating: "Regarding the loan from Xigang Company to Party B, the parties entered into the 'Agreement' on June 13, 2014, and the 'Supplement Agreement' on August 13, 2015, respectively, which clearly stipulated the loan issue and the equity matters of Harbin Longjun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longjun Company). To ensure the realization of Party B's creditor's rights, on June 12, 2014, Party A transferred 100% of the equity in Longjun Company to Party B and completed the procedures for the change of equity. Given that Party A is still in a period of rectification and recovery, as of the date of this agreement, Party A has still not repaid the loan. To further clarify the rights and obligations of the parties, based on the principles of equality, mutual benefit, and consensus, the parties have reached the following agreement. 1. Handling of creditor's rights and debts and confirmation of equity. 1.1 Pursuant to Article 1 of the 'Supplement Agreement' signed on August 13, 2015, Party A borrowed RMB 447,159,452.22 from Liu Zhiping, and at the same time received a payment of RMB 43,594,471.52 from Liu Zhiping for the temporary transfer of 100% of the equity in Longjun Company. The total principal is tentatively set at RMB 490,753,923.74, with the exact amount to be confirmed by the parties after reconciliation. Additionally, RMB 650,000 in attorney fees and other fees paid by Liu Zhiping on behalf of Xigang Company constitutes a creditor's right of Liu Zhiping. 1.2 Party A agrees to use 100% of the equity and assets of Longjun Company to offset the debt, with the offset amount to be determined in accordance with Article 2.3 of this Agreement. 1.3 Given that the parties have already completed the procedures for the change of equity transfer on June 12, 2014, both parties unanimously confirm that the equity change is valid and that there is no need to repeat the change procedures. 1.4 The portion of Party B's creditor's rights not satisfied or the portion by which the offset amount exceeds its creditor's rights shall still be handled in accordance with the original 'Agreement' and 'Supplement Agreement,' and shall be supplemented or reduced from the value of 64% of the equity in Xunke County Cuihongshan Mining Co., Ltd. pledged to Liu Zhiping. ... 2.1 Both parties jointly select an asset appraisal institution to assess the assets of Longjun Company. ... The scope of the asset appraisal shall not include the 262 units of collectively constructed housing (attach a detailed list of properties including owners, buildings, floors, units, room numbers, and areas as an appendix to this Agreement) and 98 parking spaces that were pre-sold to Party A's employees under the 'Agreement' and 'Supplement Agreement' signed on June 13, 2014, and August 13, 2015 ... The appraisal base date is April 30, 2017. ... 3.1 After this Agreement takes effect, Party A transfers 100% of the equity in Longjun Company to Party B, and the corresponding amount of Party B's creditor's rights is offset; Party B enjoys all the rights and obligations of a shareholder of Longjun Company in accordance with the law, and Party B is responsible for the subsequent investment, construction, management, and completion of the acceptance procedures for Longjun Company ... 3.2.2 Within 10 working days after the signing of this Agreement, Party A shall deliver to Party B the electronic and paper original files of all archive materials of Longjun Company, including various approval documents, various contracts and agreements such as construction and procurement, financial vouchers, construction drawings, and marked maps of the locations of pre-sold properties."

本院认为，上述约定的核心内容为，“甲方同意以龙郡公司100%的股权及资产抵债”、“鉴于2014年6月12日双方已经办理了股权转让变更手续，双方一致确认该股权变更有效，不需要再次履行变更手续。”“乙方债权未获清偿部分或抵债金额超过其债权的部分，依然按照原《协议书》及《补充协议书》中的约定办理，从质押给刘志平的逊克县翠宏山矿业有限公司64%股权价值中补足或冲减。”“双方共同选定资产评估机构对龙郡公司资产进行评估。”“本协议生效后，甲方将龙郡公司100%的股权转让给乙方，乙方享有的相应数额债权得以抵销，乙方依法享有龙郡公司股东全部权利义务。”据此，因债务人西钢公司借期内未能偿还借款本息，在担保基础上作出的上述约定，旨在以龙郡公司100%股权抵债以实现债权。此时，西钢公司与刘志平（闽成公司）已就真实转让龙郡公司100%股权达成合意，西钢公司有义务向刘志平（闽成公司）移交龙郡公司100%股权。西钢公司与刘志平约定，对确切债权金额对账、双方在评估价基础上确定龙郡公司资产价值，为有关股权抵债计算方式的约定，而非抵债协议生效条件。西钢公司上诉提出，龙郡公司股权变更协议并非为抵偿债务、以龙郡公司股权抵债条件尚不具备等主张，与约定不符，与事实不符，本院不予支持。

2017年10月18日，东宇公司出具《资产评估报告》。主要内容为：受刘志平、西钢公司委托，以2017年4月30日为评估基准日，对龙郡公司的哈市群力西钢大厦在建工程、西钢大厦地下车位、西钢嘉苑A、B栋部分在建工程、哈市阿城区黑纺路土地使用权及部分债权债务进行评估，评估有效期为2017年4月30日至2018年4月29日。《资产评估报告》第12页记载：“委估资产账面净值435751003元，评估值362043732元，减值额73707271元。”第13页记载：“根据委托方提供的资料，西钢大厦超建筑面积尚未办妥手续，停工后施工方与建设方存在索赔不确定因素较多，存在不可预见支出事项。因此，办理超建筑面积5783平方米处罚手续费用暂按51740000元估算，停工索赔费用暂按51692226元估算。待工程结束后，由甲乙方按实际支出协商解决。”本院认为，上述履约行为旨在落实“双方共同选定资产评估机构对龙郡公司资产进行评估”等约定内容。西钢公司上诉主张，评估范围仅包含龙郡公司部分资产，闽成公司主张抵偿龙郡公司100%股权，故，应在评估价基础上双方进一步商议具体抵偿金额和抵偿方式。评估报告将龙郡房地产项目中未决事项、法律纠纷等不确定因素，列支为办理超建筑面积5783平方米处罚金额暂按51740000元估算、停工索赔费用暂按51692226元估算，两项合计1亿余元，作为不可预见支出项目从龙郡公司股权评估价中扣减，存在虚高且缺乏依据。本院认为，就对龙郡公司股权价值的评估范围，西钢公司与刘志平及龙郡公司于2017年5月15日签订的协议第2.1条明确约定，“评估资产范围不包括双方2014年6月13日、2015年8月13日签订的《协议书》《补充协议书》中规定的已预售给甲方员工的集资建房的房产262户和车位98个……。伊春市西林区龙郡公司名下所有资产不纳入本次评估范围。”刘志平与西钢公司签约约定，以龙郡公司100%股权作为让与担保标的物以保证借款债权实现；直至以龙郡公司100%股权变价折抵债权的《资产评估报告》作出后，西钢公司才就评估范围等提出异议。西钢公司上诉提出的主张，显与其在系列合同中作出的意思表示不符，与其在担保物评估变价期间的态度不符，也未提供相应证据佐证其观点，本院不予采信。本案二审中各方均同意将龙郡公司评估价值从362043732元，调整为464541718元。龙郡公司及其项下房地产项目的实际控制权已移转至闽成公司，已由闽成公司接盘并接续开发建设。故，应从闽成公司对西钢公司享有的债权本息中相应扣减464541718元。同时，本院认为，如日后发生超建筑面积处罚、停工索赔等新增费用，应依约另行据实核算，权利人就此享有诉权。一审判决认定，双方当事人均对龙郡公司已由闽成公司实际接收控制均无异议，即该抵债行为已实际履行完毕；协议明确约定伊春市西林区龙郡公司名下所有资产不纳入本次评估范围，债权债务由西钢公司负担。对一审上述认定，本院认可。

西钢公司还主张，西钢公司已进入破产重整程序，以龙郡公司股权作价抵顶西钢公司对闽成公司债务，损害其他债权人权益。本院认为，《破产法》第三十条规定，破产申请受理时属于债务人的全部财产，以及破产申请受理后至破产程序终结前债务人取得的财产，为债务人财产。为防止债务人不当减少责任财产而损害全体债权人利益，《破产法》第十六条规定，人民法院受理破产申请后，债务人对个别债权人的债务清偿无效；第三十一条规定，破产申请前一年内发生的无偿转让财产等涉及债务人财产的特定行为，管理人有权请求人民法院予以撤销；第三十二条规定，人民法院受理破产申请前六个月内，如债务人已达到破产界限仍对个别债权人清偿，除该个别清偿使债务人财产受益的情形之外，管理人亦有权请求人民法院予以撤销。本案一审中，黑龙江省伊春市中级人民法院于2018年6月11日作出（2018）黑07破申1号民事裁定，受理西钢公司重整申请。本院认为，2017年5月15日西钢公司、刘志平与龙郡公司签订协议的第1.2条载明，“甲方同意以龙郡公司100%的股权及资产抵债”；1.3条载明，“鉴于2014年6月12日双方已经办理了股权转让变更手续，双方一致确认该股权变更有效，不需要再次履行变更手续”等。可见，以龙郡公司股权抵债行为发生于2017年5月15日，即龙郡公司100%股权亦于同日转移至刘志平名下，年底前已依约完成抵债股权评估。换言之，在黑龙江省伊春市中级人民法院受理西钢公司破产重整申请一年之前，龙郡公司股权已不属于西钢公司责任财产，以龙郡公司股权抵债并非《破产法》第十六条所指的人民法院受理破产申请后债务人对个别债权人清偿行为，亦不属《破产法》第三十一条规定、第三十二条规定的可撤销行为。西钢公司提出的前述主张，与本案事实不符，于法无据，本院不予支持。

三、闽成公司是否有权就翠宏山公司64%股权优先受偿

2014年6月20日，西钢公司为甲方、刘志平为乙方签订《协议书》，约定：“甲方向乙方借款用于银行短期倒贷，本息合计723606136.82元（股权比例计算说明见附件一）。现由于甲方无力偿还，西钢公司同意将其持有翠宏山公司64%股权转让给刘志平，乙方。现甲乙双方经协商一致，就未尽事宜达成协议如下：……二、甲乙双方签订的股权转让协议的目的是以股权转让的形式保证乙方债权的实现，督促甲方按本协议的约定偿还乙方的借款。本协议约定的还款期限为：2014年6月21日至2015年6月20日。……四、在本协议约定的还款期限内，甲乙双方应保证：1、甲方应积极筹措资金偿还乙方借款，每偿还一笔借款，按还款数额相应核减乙方的持股比例。当投入逊克县翠宏山矿业有限公司的借款本息723606136.82元、投入西钢集团哈尔滨龙郡房地产开发有限公司借款490753923.74元、西林钢铁集团有限公司借款100000000.00元全部还清时，乙方应将受让的逊克县翠宏山矿业有限公司的股权份额全部转回甲方或甲方指定的公司，并配合甲方办理工商变更登记手续。……五、如甲方在本协议约定的还款期限内未能偿还乙方的借款时：……利息按原借款合同约定的税后年息18%计算，按月支付。”为履行上述约定内容，2014年6月13日，翠宏山公司股东会决议同意西钢公司将其所持有的翠宏山公司64%股权转让给刘志平，其他股东放弃优先购买权。西钢公司与翠宏山公司在工商部门办理了翠宏山公司股东变更登记。

2015年8月13日，西钢公司为甲方、刘志平为乙方，签订《补充协议书》，约定：“甲、乙双方于2014年6月20日签订逊克县翠宏山矿业有限公司股权转让协议书，甲方将持有的翠宏山矿业公司64%的股权未按对价原则阶段性转让给乙方，以保证乙方债权的安全和实现。鉴于现阶段甲方尚无力偿付对乙方的债务并回购翠宏山矿业公司64%的股权，且乙方也没有实质持有翠宏山矿业公司股权的意愿，为此，甲、乙双方基于实际考虑，经协商一致，达成补充协议如下：……二、甲乙双方1年内引进战略投资商投资翠宏山时，战略投资商用于购买乙方阶段性持有的翠宏山矿业公司股权的价款，首先用于偿还甲方对乙方的借款本息，乙方按还款比例相应减持64%股权比例，同时对已偿还借款停止计息。……四、若从补充协议签订之日起，1年内甲方不能全部还清债务，乙方有权对外出售翠宏山矿业公司股权，出售价格以评估价格为基础下浮不超过10%；出售股权比例变现的额度，不得超过未清偿借款本息和。同等条件甲方有优先回购权。五、截至2015年6月20日，甲方向乙方借款本息合计849232648.54元。若6个月内清偿，按年税后利率12%付息；若还款期限超过6个月部分，按年税后利率18%付息。利息一年一结算。六、乙方在哈尔滨龙郡房地产有限公司债权未清偿部分转入翠宏山矿业公司64%股权中，在翠宏山矿业公司股权变卖所得价款中清偿。”

本院认为，西钢公司与刘志平签订的《协议书》约定，“双方签订的股权转让协议的目的是以股权转让的形式保证乙方债权的实现，督促甲方按本协议的约定偿还乙方的借款。”“甲方应积极筹措资金偿还乙方借款，每偿还一笔借款，按还款数额相应核减乙方的持股比例。”“……全部还清时，乙方应将受让的逊克县翠宏山矿业有限公司的股权份额全部转回甲方或甲方指定的公司，并配合甲方办理工商变更登记手续”。《补充协议书》再次明确，该股权转让是为了“保证乙方债权的安全和实现”，且双方确认“乙方也没有实质持有翠宏山矿业公司股权的意愿”。可见，双方签订股权转让协议的目的是以股权转让形式保证刘志平债权的实现，担保西钢公司按协议约定偿还借款。上述《协议书》《补充协议书》约定将西钢公司名下翠宏山公司64%股权变更至刘志平名下，与前述以龙郡公司100%股权提供担保为同一性质的担保，并非真正的股权转让，而是将翠宏山公司64%股权作为对刘志平债权实现的非典型担保，即让与担保。对此，各方不持异议。如前所述，有关让与担保的约定内容真实、自愿、合法，不具有合同无效情形，应为有效合同。一审判决认定，双方于2014年6月13日签订《协议书》、2015年8月13日签订《补充协议书》的真实目的并非真正实现股权转让，而是为了对案涉债务提供担保，符合本案当事人在相关系列合同中作出的连贯的、一致的真实意思表示，本院予以确认。西钢公司主张，上述《协议书》《补充协议书》系本案各方通谋虚伪意思表示，依据《民法总则》第一百四十六条规定和《破产法》相关规定，应属无效。对西钢公司提出的该项诉请，不予支持。

本院认为，与认定以龙郡公司100%股权设立让与担保的约定有效同理，亦应认定以翠宏山公司64%股权设立的让与担保约定有效。《民法总则》第一百四十六条规定，行为人与相对人以虚假的意思表示实施的民事法律行为无效。以虚假的意思表示隐藏的民事法律行为的效力，依照有关法律规定处理。是否为“以虚假的意思表示实施的民事法律行为”，应当结合当事人在主合同即借款合同和从合同即让与担保合同中作出的真实意思表示，统筹作出判断。约定将债务人或第三人股权转让给债权人的合同目的是设立担保，翠宏山公司64%股权转让至闽成公司代持股人刘志平名下是为西钢公司向闽成公司的巨额借款提供担保，而非设立股权转让民事关系。对此，债权人、债务人明知。从这一角度看，债权人、债务人的真实意思是以向债权人转让翠宏山公司股权的形式为债权实现提供担保，“显现的”是转让股权，“隐藏的”是为借款提供担保而非股权转让，均为让与担保既有法律特征的有机组成部分,均是债权人、债务人的真实意思，该意思表示不存在不真实或不一致的瑕疵，也未违反法律、行政法规的效力性强制性规定。

西钢公司上诉主张，以翠宏山公司股权设定的让与担保违反物权法定及物权公示原则，违反法律禁止流押流质的规定。本院认为，首先，根据物权和债权区分原则，物权法定原则并不能否定上述合同的效力，即使股权让与担保不具有物权效力，股权让与担保合同也不必然无效。其次，让与担保虽非《物权法》等法律规定的有名担保，但属在法理及司法实践中得到广泛确认的非典型担保。本院认为，《物权法》第一百八十六条规定，抵押权人在债务履行期届满前，不得与抵押人约定债务人不履行到期债务时抵押财产归债权人所有；第二百一十一条规定，质权人在债务履行期届满前，不得与出质人约定债务人不履行到期债务时质押财产归债权人所有。前述《物权法》禁止流押、禁止流质之规定，旨在避免债权人乘债务人之危而滥用其优势地位，压低担保物价值，谋取不当利益。如约定担保权人负有清算义务，当债务人不履行债务时，担保权人并非当然取得担保物所有权时，并不存在流押、流质的问题。本案中，西钢公司与刘志平2015年8月13日签订的《补充协议书》约定，如西钢公司不能还清债务，“乙方有权对外出售翠宏山矿业公司股权，出售价格以评估价格为基础下浮不超过10%；出售股权比例变现的额度，不得超过未清偿借款本息。”可见，西钢公司与刘志平就以翠宏山公司64%股权设定的让与担保，股权出售价格应以“评估价格为基础下浮不超过10%”的清算方式变现。本院认为，上述约定不违反禁止流质流押的法律规定，应当认定上述约定有效。

Mincheng Company appealed, arguing that transfer for security is a non-typical security interest recognized by the Private Lending Provisions, and the purpose of establishing such security is to allow the creditor to obtain priority satisfaction from the secured subject matter. The 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company involved in the case had been registered with the industry and commerce department under the name of Liu Zhiping, which has the effect of public notice of real rights and can be invoked against third parties, and can restrict the transfer or other disposition of such equity. Therefore, Mincheng Company claimed that it had a priority real right over the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company that could exclude third parties. Xigang Company argued that, under the principle of numerus clausus of real rights, only categories of real rights expressly provided for by law can have the effect of real rights recognized and protected by law. Transfer for security is not a category of real rights expressly provided for by law; it only has the effect of creditor's rights and does not have the same effect of real rights as statutory real rights, cannot be invoked against third parties, and cannot obtain priority in satisfaction over other creditors. From the content of the contracts, neither the Agreement nor the Supplemental Agreement, which established the transfer for security over the equity, stipulated that Liu Zhiping had a right to priority satisfaction. We hold that the substantive focus of the dispute between Mincheng Company and Xigang Company is: whether the transfer for security established over the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company has the effect of a real right, and whether the holder of the transfer for security can thereby obtain the right to priority satisfaction from the value of that equity. Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Opinions on Further Strengthening Financial Trial Work stipulates that the legal validity of new types of security should be determined in accordance with law, so as to broaden the financing guarantee methods for small and medium-sized micro enterprises. Except where the contract falls under the circumstances of invalidity under Article 52 of the Contract Law, new types of security contracts should be determined valid in accordance with law; if they also meet the provisions of the Property Law on security real rights, their effect as real rights should also be determined in accordance with law. As to whether the aforementioned transfer for security over equity has the effect of a real right, the core criterion should be whether it has been publicized in accordance with the principle of publicity of real rights. In the transfer for security at issue in this case, the secured subject matter is the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company. Article 32, paragraph 2 of the Company Law of the PRC provides that a company shall register the names or titles of its shareholders with the company registration authority; if the registered items change, the change shall be registered. Without registration or change registration, it cannot be invoked against third parties. Thus, change of registration with the company registration authority is the method of publicity for changes in company equity. Articles 208(1), 226(1) and 229 of the Property Law provide that in an equity pledge, the pledgee may obtain priority satisfaction from the equity for which a pledge registration has been effected. By reasoning from the lesser to the greater, in a transfer for security of equity where the equity serving as security property has been registered in the name of the security holder, the security holder is formally already the holder of the shares that are the subject matter of the security. The right of the security holder to priority satisfaction from the equity serving as security should be even more protected, and in principle has the effect of a real right that can be invoked against third parties. This is precisely the core value of transfer for security of equity. In this case, Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping entered into the Agreement in June 2014 to establish a transfer for security over the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company. The creditor Mincheng Company, through its nominee shareholder Liu Zhiping, coordinated with the debtor Xigang Company and completed the change of registration of the company's shareholders as agreed, and formally Liu Zhiping became the transferee of that equity. Therefore, the security right that Liu Zhiping enjoyed under the agreement is superior to ordinary creditor's rights and has the effect of a real right that can be invoked against other ordinary creditors of Xigang Company. Mincheng Company's claim that Liu Zhiping has the right to priority satisfaction from the 64% equity in Cuihongshan Company is supported by us. Xigang Company's argument, that transfer for security is not a statutory real right and that the parties to the contract did not stipulate that Liu Zhiping had a right to priority satisfaction, to deny its claim for priority satisfaction, is not supported by us. The first instance judgment's finding that the transfer for security did not have the effect of a real right and could not be invoked against third parties was erroneous, and we correct it.

Mincheng Company argued that the first instance judgment, by invoking Article 16 of the Bankruptcy Law regarding the prohibition of individual satisfaction, refused to support its claim for priority satisfaction from the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company, which was an error in the application of law. It should have been determined, in accordance with Article 109 of the Bankruptcy Law, that it enjoyed the right to priority satisfaction. Xigang Company argued that only holders of statutory security real rights under the Property Law and the Security Law can enjoy the right to priority satisfaction in bankruptcy proceedings under Article 109 of the Bankruptcy Law; if Liu Zhiping were adjudged to have a right to priority satisfaction from the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company, it would harm the interests of other creditors and adversely affect the bankruptcy reorganization of Xigang Company and 40 other companies. We hold that determining that Liu Zhiping has a right to priority satisfaction from the equity in dispute does not constitute an individual satisfaction act under Article 16 of the Bankruptcy Law. The reason Article 16 of the Bankruptcy Law provides that individual satisfaction acts after the people's court accepts a bankruptcy application are invalid is, first, because such individual satisfaction acts reduce the total amount of bankruptcy property; and second, because such individual satisfaction acts violate the principle of fair satisfaction. Where the parties establish a transfer for security over equity and complete the corresponding change of registration of the equity, and the transferor in the transfer for security enters bankruptcy proceedings, determining that the holder of the transfer for security has a right to priority satisfaction from the equity on which the transfer for security has been established is the existing function of the legal institution of transfer for security and is the purpose of establishing the transfer for security contract.

In this case, the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company had been registered in the name of Liu Zhiping, and Liu Zhiping had a right to priority satisfaction from that equity. According to the evidence on file, although the series of loan contracts, debt-offsetting agreements, the agreement establishing a transfer for security over the equity of Cuihongshan Company, and the supplemental agreements were all signed in the name of Liu Zhiping with Xigang Company, bank transfer records and other relevant evidence show that, except for the loans provided by Guan Wenji and Lu Zhiguo, the other loans were all remitted from the accounts of Mincheng Company or its affiliates (Mingqi Company, Minlong Company). Guan Wenji and Lu Zhiguo each assigned their claims to Liu Zhiping. Liu Zhiping himself also admitted that the true right holder was Mincheng Company, and the shares of Cuihongshan Company under his name were merely held on behalf of Mincheng Company. In light of this, given that there is a genuine creditor-debtor relationship between Mincheng Company and Xigang Company, and there is no dispute between Mincheng Company and Liu Zhiping regarding the shareholding-on-behalf relationship, Mincheng Company's claim to priority satisfaction from the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company should be supported.

In this second instance, all parties confirmed that, with the consent of Liu Zhiping, the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company involved in the case had been used as a pledge to secure a financial loan of Xigang Company from the non-party Minsheng Bank Dalian Branch. In the case of Minsheng Bank Dalian Branch v. Xigang Company, Yichun Baijia Industrial Co., Ltd., Liu Zhiping, Sichuan Dazhou Iron and Steel Group Co., Ltd., and Cuihongshan Company concerning a dispute over a financial loan contract, the Liaoning High People's Court rendered the first instance civil judgment (2017) Liao Min Chu No. 44 on October 17, 2017, which has now come into legal effect. Minsheng Bank Dalian Branch has a right to priority satisfaction from the pledged property within the scope of the principal debt of RMB 500 million and the corresponding interest, overdue interest, compound interest, and costs of realizing the claim, in respect of the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company held by Liu Zhiping. We hold that Mincheng Company has a right to priority satisfaction from the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company. Given that all parties in this case confirmed that, with the consent of Liu Zhiping, the equity that had been transferred as security to secure Mincheng Company's claim was further pledged to the creditor bank of Xigang Company, Minsheng Bank Dalian Branch should be satisfied from the 64% equity of Cuihongshan Company in priority to Liu Zhiping (Mincheng Company).

IV. Whether the First Instance Procedure of This Case Was Lawful

To prove that the eight Loan Contracts involved in the case were not signed on the dates recorded in the contract documents or were signed before the transfer of remittance, Xigang Company applied for a document examination in both the first and second instances to determine whether the eight Loan Contracts were formed at the same time. We hold that, as stated above, the lender had actually paid the agreed loan to the borrower Xigang Company, and Xigang Company has not yet repaid. Whether the signing dates of the eight Loan Contracts are before or after payment does not affect the formation, validity, or performance of the private lending contract, and there is indeed no need to submit them for document examination. The first instance finding that "even if an examination were conducted, it would not be able to prove that the agreements involved were not the true expression of the parties' intent, and this court does not support Xigang Company's defense on this point" is affirmed by us.

In the first and second instances, Liu Zhiping appeared in person or authorized a legal representative attorney to appear in court, and his coherent, clear, and consistent expression of intent was: Liu Zhiping's personal identity is that of an employee of a subsidiary of Mincheng Company. All the Loan Agreements, Supplemental Agreements, and Debt-Offsetting Agreements signed in the name of Liu Zhiping with Xigang Company were signed on behalf of Mincheng Company, and the resulting claims and equity all belong to Mincheng Company. Liu Zhiping himself does not have the ability to lend the large sums involved in this case, has no business dealings with the parties, and does not assert any rights over all the loans and equity involved. At the second instance trial, the authorized agent of Mincheng Company supplemented his defense by stating: "This case is not a case related to identity; all the facts of the case were stated by Liu Zhiping when he appeared in court on the two previous occasions, he submitted a written defense, and he also authorized a lawyer to appear on his behalf." Liu Zhiping, as a third party in this case, has participated in the litigation of this case through various statutory forms, lawfully and properly exercised his right of action, fully expressed his own demands, and there is no procedural defect or flaw. The court does not need to collect evidence from him ex officio. Xigang Company appealed, arguing that the first instance court did not respond to Xigang Company's requests for Liu Zhiping to appear in person and for the court to question Liu Zhiping ex officio based on the examination outline submitted by Xigang Company, resulting in a lack of evidence to support the factual allegations it raised, which in turn led to erroneous findings of fact in the first instance. We hold that, in the first and second instances, Liu Zhiping personally or through his attorney appeared in court to participate in the litigation. The people's court should respect Liu Zhiping's lawful exercise of his right of action in an appropriate manner. Whether Liu Zhiping personally appears in court does not affect the ascertainment of the facts of the case. Article 174 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides that a defendant who must appear in court refers to a defendant who has obligations to provide support, raise, or foster, and where the facts cannot be ascertained without the defendant's appearance. Liu Zhiping's procedural status in the first instance was that of a third party. Whether he is a third party with an independent claim or a third party without an independent claim, under the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law and the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, Liu Zhiping is not a party who must appear in court.

Xigang Company requested a stay of proceedings in this case, on the grounds that Dongxing Company, on September 11, 2018, filed case (2018) Hei 07 Min Chu No. 32 with the Yichun Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province, seeking to rescind the series of Debt-Offsetting Agreements, Loan Contracts, and the Agreement for transfer for security of equity dated June 13 and June 20, 2014, between Xigang Company and Liu Zhiping. Mincheng Company argued that the non-party Dongxing Company had filed two cases related to this case in a separate action. The Xilin District People's Court of Yichun City accepted the cases but did not hear them, dragging on for seven months; thereafter, Dongxing Company withdrew the lawsuits. In September 2018, Dongxing Company again filed a lawsuit with the Yichun Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province on the same grounds; similarly, the court accepted the case but did not hear it, and service has not yet been completed. Since the filing dates of these cases were later than the filing date of this case, and the causes of action are different, they should not be grounds for staying this case. We hold that, under Article 150(1)(5) of the Civil Procedure Law, the trial of this case does not require that the outcome of case (2018) Hei 07 Min Chu No. 32 be determined first, and this case does not fall under the circumstances where proceedings should be stayed. Xigang Company's claim that this case should be stayed cannot be upheld. The first instance trial procedure was lawful, and we affirm it.
